correctness.rationale: The determinant has exactly a diagonal-product term and one directed-cycle term. Frobenius splitting and separability characterize all allowed products and diagonal multisets; orbit frequencies follow by explicit edge-gauge transitivity, period Möbius inversion, and Burnside. Nonzero Krylov pivots give nilpotency index n. The independent finite-field enumeration and direct matrix powers in verify.py reproduce all asserted finite instances.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Theorem 4.6 in 2009 is exactly the support/existence theorem, so repeating it would be covered. Its conclusion “at least one realization” does not determine how many labelled choices or which monomial stabilizers occur. Engel–Schneider’s canonical gauge form explains when edges have the same product but does not determine which diagonal words are nilpotent or their periods. The present claim is the complete product of those new quantitative analyses, with explicit all-parameter orbit sizes and multiplicities.

value.rationale: The known existence criterion says only whether at least one nilpotent realization occurs. The exact count, density, and complete stabilizer/orbit distribution answer natural additional invariants of the same irreducible support family for all dimensions and prime powers. The inseparable strata produce genuine mixed rotation periods: over F4 at n=6 there are 2 small and 14 large orbits, which existence and Jordan type cannot distinguish.
